claim: Introducing multiple agents for cross-verification in a multi-agent system can lead to consensus on incorrect solutions due to reinforcement of shared biases or conflict that requires human intervention.
falsifier: In a multi-agent system for scientific discovery, compare the accuracy of consensus solutions when using single-agent versus multi-agent cross-verification, measuring the frequency of incorrect consensus and human intervention needed.

conditions: when agents are built on large language models with limitations in factual accuracy and reliability
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Introducing multiple agents–consensus on correctness boundary

claim: Larger multi-agent teams require more discussion turns and face coordination challenges, but multi-agent teams outperform single agents; excessively large teams may encounter communication barriers.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by systematically varying team size and measuring discussion turns, coordination metrics, and output quality.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system, task, team sizes (4 and 8 members), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Team size–discussion turns required, coordination boundary
